summary: Lincoln County, MT tower with an L-4 cab, built 1934 and abandoned by the late 1960s; registered 2000; FireLookout.com alone says it burned in 2014.

facts.design: 10-foot pole tower with an L-4 cab
facts.status_note: FireLookout.com says the tower burned in summer 2014; this is the only source read for the fire. No source describes the peak today.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register gives 4,756 ft (1,450 m), matching the record's 1449.6 m. FireLookout.com gives 4820 ft, which does not match; the record value is kept.

sources.title: Montana Lookouts, Forest Fire Lookout Association

notes_for_editor: The 2014 burn rests on one source, FireLookout.com. A Libby news update from August 2014 (libbymt.com/news/2014/08/Wildfireupdate.htm) that may cover it could not be read: fetch_text got an SSL certificate error, the http version returned 404, and WebFetch also failed on the certificate. Worth retrying by hand. A 2026 Watch Duty incident named 'D5 Tony Peak Fire' near Jennings Haul Rd, Libby (July 2026) shares the peak's name; it is not linked to the lookout and is not used. Elevation: FireLookout.com 4820 ft vs NHLR 4,756 ft (1,450 m) and record 1449.6 m; record kept. The Forest Lookouts page for Tony Peak has only a legal description (30N-29W-19) and no narrative. No access or current-site information was found, so access is left out. The story is short because the evidence is thin.
